analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/reference/protocol-messages.md. It adds an 'Add-on hold busy fields' section (head 171-195) and table rows for register (head 284) and heartbeat (head 383). It also adds `addon_hold` to the ModelAutopilotBusyReason list (head 1445) and updates the date (head 3).

The documented behavior is as follows. While a local add-on holds the Mac, the provider stays registered and reports heartbeat status=draining with optional busy_reason, busy_since_ms and busy_addon fields; register carries the same fields. Coordinator routing exclusion relies on the existing draining status (applyHeartbeatDrainStateLocked, base 345). Requests routed during a hold get the typed draining rejection, and an unknown busy_reason decodes to absent.

The hold deliberately bypasses the provider_drain barrier and resumes on the same connection with its next idle or serving heartbeat. Base 136-140 already notes that a stale idle heartbeat cannot reopen a connection fenced by provider_drain; the hold uses only the softer heartbeat mark, so this does not weaken the barrier. These fields are untrusted provider self-reports. The doc states no authorization or billing meaning for them (TB-002, TB-011), and this file adds no new grant semantics.

No concrete regression is visible: no source is changed here, and the cited Swift files are not supplied. Questions for integration and source review:
(1) The add-on hold IPC (docs/architecture/addon-hold.md, ProviderBusy.swift) is new local attack surface not in the threat model. Which local processes can assert or release a hold? Is the add-on's code-signing identity verified or self-claimed? (Relevant to TB-003 and the TB-010-style local helper boundary.)
(2) Does starting a hold wait for, or cancel, in-flight decrypted inference? Does it also clear GPU/KV memory before the add-on (for example io.darkbloom.sandbox) gets the machine? (A-001, T-028, T-041.)
(3) busy_addon exposes add-on identity to the coordinator and possibly to telemetry or the console (T-058 linkage). It should be bounded and sanitized.
(4) Are busy fields placed outside the signed or raw-attestation register bytes? Registration should not change canonical signatures (encodeRegisterPreservingRawAttestation).
(5) Will the threat model need an entry for the add-on hold boundary?
